PLC and remote-I/O data links drive the registered control-valve control inputs. Loss of PLC or I/O communication removes their modeled throughput. This is an illustrative availability gate, not a safety PLC program or validated control loop.
The generic I/O family response is held at a high normalized demand so a healthy upstream PLC leaves positive valve capacity; this is not a real I/O transfer function.
Move grain through milling, mash separation, cooling, fermentation and packaging. Effluent and heat service remain independent utility branches.
All quantities are editable normalized placeholders. Stage names do not supply a production recipe, validated quality criterion or real protection setting.
Material, electrical, thermal, data and measurement connections have separate roles. The external model owns one shared state and clock for every view.
Repair clears component damage; it does not undo intentionally changed load, valves, capacity or other operating inputs.
Optional utility skids illustrate dependency plumbing and are not claims about standard industry equipment or energy performance.

Instruments use explicit measurement taps on equipment outlet or vessel readings; they do not create a material sink or claim physical inline pressure loss. All displayed measurements remain normalized estimates.

PLC and remote-I/O data links drive the registered control-valve control inputs. Loss of PLC or I/O communication removes their modeled throughput. This is an illustrative availability gate, not a safety PLC program or validated control loop.
Pumps and generators retain local operator enable commands. Their electrical drive ports are not misrepresented as PLC data inputs; no automatic start, transfer or synchronization is implemented.
The auxiliary generator is a continuously enabled independent supply with assumed fuel. It is not an automatic standby-transfer system.
